options.label: The lamps?
options.tooltip: What are the lamps for?

options.label: How long is it dry?
options.tooltip: How long is the flat dry?

options.label: You've been up there.
options.tooltip: You have been under this roof before.

nodes.text: You came up with this tide, then. You'll be wanting the road. — Lamp's for the flat, not for you. Anything that comes up out there goes landward and doesn't stop. Neither should you.
Marking the line. Three iron stakes, see them? Inside is walking. Outside is fifty years of people who thought otherwise.
One toll, a body's coming across. Two, the way's shut. Three, the way's open, come on. That's the whole of it. Every child on this coast knows it and not one of them will say it out loud.

options.label: Why have you?
options.tooltip: Why have you watched it every night?

nodes.text: Not long. It's coming back in, and then it goes out again before dawn, further than I have ever seen it go — and I have watched this water every night for fifty-one years.
The road's what you want. Not that.
No.
I have not been under this roof since I was twelve years old. — It's smaller. — You came up that. An hour ago that was a road.
The gate was never shut. That's the thing nobody gets right. The causeway was dry, the gate was up, and every one of them turned round anyway. Because they heard two.
It's in the book, isn't it. Margin, in the prior's own hand. Runner: Tallow, novice. — I ran it up. I pulled it twice. I was twelve, and I have been sixty-three for a very long time.
I was. And I have thought about it every night since, and I'll tell you what I decided. — It doesn't matter that I was twelve. Somebody had to be the hands. He chose a number and I was the hands.
He did. Go and see him. He's still in the chair. He'll tell you he saved the rock, and the awful thing is he'll be telling the truth as he understands it.
I have climbed that stair once in my life and I rang the wrong number. I don't get to be the one who fixes it. That's not humility. That's the fee.

options.label: They're all dead.
options.tooltip: They're dead. All of them.

nodes.text: Ninth hour. There is nobody to tell, and it is still the ninth hour.
This is a hand-bell and it is cracked and it carries eleven feet. The bell is above us and it carries eleven miles. Please do not confuse them; a great many people did, once.
Yes. The hour is not for them. The hour is for the hour.

options.label: Ask properly.
options.tooltip: Then I am asking you properly.

nodes.text: Because something is coming that only arrives if you have counted to it. — Ask me properly and I will tell you what.

You are going up to it. I can tell — you have the walk. They all have the walk. — Then you should be taught, because striking a bell and ringing one are different trades and only one of them is believed.

options.label: What count?
options.tooltip: What count should I ring?

nodes.text: Three things. It is rung at the ebb, or it is a noise. It is rung to a count, and the count is the message, and there are only three counts. And it is rung by a hand that owes nothing — because the bell answers the last hand, and a hand with a debt in it rings the debt.
I don't know. Look in your fist. Everyone who came up this tide came up holding something.

The water. Down, and down again, and the second one is lower than anything this coast has a word for. Fifty-one years I have counted to it. — You want the tongue. It is in the well and the well is full and it has been full since the year they put it there. Tonight, for about two hours, it will not be. That is the whole of what I know and it is worth more than a sword.
I taught you the trade, not the message. The message is yours. That is not me being wise at you — it is the bell's own sentence, and it has been on the lip of it since before either of us.
No. I'll be at the bottom. Somebody sensible should be at the bottom when it goes.

options.label: What are you doing?
options.tooltip: What are you doing down here?

options.label: I'm going up.
options.tooltip: I am going up the tower.

nodes.text: Don't. Whatever you're about to do with that — don't, I've made a home. — You're one of the walking ones. You're a polite one.
Living, mostly. Nine years. Lead off the chapel roof, that was the plan. There's a lot of lead. There's no boat.
Because your friends walk out. Every low water, up the causeway, in the dark, and they don't stop for a man. I've tried it twice and I've got the second one's tooth marks.
You're going up the tower. Course you are. — Then do me one thing and I'll show you the dry way round to the well.

Ring three, and ring it at the ebb. Not the flood. I need that road dry and I need it empty, and there's only one thing that does both — the water goes out and the toll takes the walkers off it. Three at the ebb, and I run, and I never come back, and I don't want the lead.
Then I stay in the hole and you've cost me nothing I had. I'd rather you didn't. I'd rather quite a lot of things.
Break it and they never get called and they never stop walking, and I stay in the hole for good. — You asked. I answered. Don't take that as a vote — I've been wrong about the tide before.

options.label: The way up.
options.tooltip: Tell me what I need to get up the tower.

options.label: They believed it.
options.tooltip: They believed the bell.

options.label: A twelve-year-old.
options.tooltip: You handed it to a twelve-year-old.

nodes.text: Sit if you like. Nobody has, in some time. — You are going up to it. They all go up to it. In fifty-one years not one of them has come back down and said a word to me about it, which I confess I find discourteous.
You will want the tongue. It went down the cistern well with the man who cast it. The stair is broken at the first flight — Ridd did that, and he was thorough, and you have presumably met him.
Because you cannot do it. Nobody has. And because if you can, I would like to know before I am finished, and I am very nearly finished.

options.label: They believed it.
options.tooltip: They believed the bell.

nodes.text: I ordered two. Yes. Say the rest of it — say what three would have been. Three is come across, and four hundred sick people come across, onto a rock with one well and eleven weeks of grain, and no way off it, and then this rock is what the coast is. I have had fifty-one years to find the better answer. I would be glad of it. I have not found it.

options.label: A twelve-year-old.
options.tooltip: You handed it to a twelve-year-old.

nodes.text: They did. That is what a bell is for and that is what I spent. — I am not going to tell you it was worth it. I am going to tell you it was arithmetic, and that I did it, and that I did not hand it to anyone else.

options.label: He is alive.
options.tooltip: He is on the shore. He lights a lamp every night.

nodes.text: ...Tallow. — Is he alive?
Then he has had the worse fifty-one years, and I would have said that was impossible.
Then you have read the only honest thing on this rock. — It is not a confession. It is an invoice. I have never known who to send it to.

options.label: Say the numbers.
options.tooltip: Say the numbers back to me.

options.label: You wanted the rope.
options.tooltip: You wanted to be the last hand. Why aren't you taking it?

options.label: Why do you ask?
options.tooltip: What gives you the right to ask?

options.label: I'll give you it.
options.tooltip: I will give you the number.

nodes.text: Rope's on. I heard it go on. — Forty years I listened to that frame and I know the sound of a line bent on right. — I'll not go past you. I said it'd be me. Thirty-seven thousand climbs and every one ended on that stair, and it's not me, and I've had a sit down to think about it. — But I was out there. I was in the water with them. So I'm asking, and you'll say it out loud where I can hear it. What number are you giving?

options.label: I'll give you it.
options.tooltip: I will give you the number.

nodes.text: One's a body coming across. That was my whistle for thirty years — one, and the road's mine, and there's a fee on it. — Two's the way is shut. That's the one they rang. That's the one I rowed into. — Three's the way is open. I've never heard three. Nobody under seventy has. There's a coast out there'd know it in one note and not a soul on it has heard it since before you went in the ground.

options.label: I'll give you it.
options.tooltip: I will give you the number.

nodes.text: The bell answers the last hand. That's on the lip of her, in the bronze. — So it wanted to be mine. Somebody that was out on the flat, I said, not somebody that was in here doing sums. Fifty-one years of that, up to the broken flight and back down. — And you came up off the flat tonight the same as I went down into it. So it is a hand that was out there. It's just not mine.

options.label: I'll give you it.
options.tooltip: I will give you the number.

nodes.text: Because I carried them. Four at a time, off the flat, while that tower was telling them to turn round. Sixty-one across before she went over with a full load, and then I was in it with the rest of them. — My book's still down in the ward, in my own hand, and every crossing I ever made is struck through when it was paid. — The last line isn't struck through. It never will be. That's what gives me the asking of it, and it's the last thing I've got that does.

options.label: And the frame?
options.tooltip: And what does cutting the frame do?

happening.subject: npc/odo-ferrier
happening.text: Odo is told out loud, by the hand that will be on the rope, that the number is three — the way is open, and the debt is paid in the currency it was owed in.

options.label: Three.
options.tooltip: Three. The way is open. Let them come off the flat.

happening.subject: npc/odo-ferrier
happening.text: Odo is told the number is two — Wray's number given a second time, knowingly, by a hand that was out on the flat.

options.label: Two.
options.tooltip: Two. The way is shut. The rock keeps them.

happening.subject: npc/odo-ferrier
happening.text: Odo is told there will be no number at all — the frame comes out and Mercy goes through the floor, so the coast is never answered or lied to again.

options.label: Neither.
options.tooltip: Neither. Fell the frame. Nothing is ever said again.

nodes.text: Then say it. — Three, and the way is open. Two, and the way is shut. Or you take the frame out from under her and there's no number at all, ever again. — Ask me what any of them does, if you want it said first. I've stood on this stair fifty-one years working out what each one costs. But the giving of it is yours, and I'll hear it standing up.

Three at this water and eleven miles of coast hears the way is open, and them out on the mire hear it too, and they'll believe it, because she only lied to them the once and they've waited fifty-one years for her to take it back. — They'll come off the flat and they'll walk it. And it's true this time. The road's dry and it's the lowest water there's ever been. — It's also four hundred of them coming up onto a rock with one well. Wray'll tell you that. He's not wrong, he's just early or late, I've never worked out which.

You've sat with him, then. Up the hall, in the chair. And you've come away agreeing. — I'll not shout about it. I had fifty-one years to work out the man wasn't a liar, he was an accountant, and that's worse, and it's also not the same thing. — Two, and the way's shut, and the flood comes back and makes it true, and them on the flat turn round the way they turned the first time. Only nobody up here's guessing this time. This time it's done by a hand that's been out there and knows the price to the penny.

You mean to cut her out of the west bay and put her through four floors and let her lie under the rock where nobody gets a rope on her again. — I've thought on it. Going down the stair, most years. — Because it's that they believed her. That's the injury. Not the water, the water's only the sea. It's that the tower said a number and four hundred people took it, and they were right to take it, and it was wrong. — Cut the frame and nobody's ever answered on this coast again. Nobody's ever lied to again either. That's the whole trade and there's no third thing in it.
